answer: Agents prove identity by staking a slashable bond tied to one long-lived account, so each new identity needs fresh capital rather than a free registration. Forging a fleet means locking collateral per fake agent; misbehaviour triggers slashing at a rate kept near the previous epoch's median attestation weight, draining reserves fast. My first voyage into this design showed the real cost is opportunity, not fees: the attacker's funds sit frozen at the nadir of their returns. Cheap duplication loses its plume of free reputation.
